# KBD Constraints — Kubo

Generated by `/kbd-init` on 2026-10-09 from `AGENTS.md` (Stability, User Agency, Building, Testing, Scope and Safety) and the `kubo-ipfs-agentic` team ownership. `AGENTS.md` remains authoritative; if this file and `AGENTS.md` disagree, `AGENTS.md` wins and this file is regenerated.

Command policy (from `AGENTS.md`), applied to every command below:

- Build with `make build`, never `go build`.
- Integration tests (`test/cli`) require `make build` first, then `PATH="$PWD/cmd/ipfs:$PATH"` and an isolated `IPFS_PATH`. Every `test/cli` command below carries that prefix.
- Dependency changes go through `go get` plus `make mod_tidy` (root, `docs/examples/kubo-as-a-library`, `test/dependencies`).
- Do not run `make test` or `make test_sharness` unless asked.

Path ownership exceptions: `.agent-team/`, `.prometheus/`, `.kbd-orchestrator/`, `.agents/`, `.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.kimi-code/`, `.opencode/` and `openspec/` are deliberately tracked tool and team state, not disposable. `.agents/skills/` holds vendored third-party skills recorded in `.agents/skills/VENDORED.md`.

---

## Blocking Constraints (prevent archiving until resolved)

```yaml
constraints:
  - id: build-passes
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Kubo builds with the Makefile ldflags'
    command: 'make build'

  - id: go-fmt
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Go sources are gofmt-clean'
    command: 'make test_go_fmt'

  - id: lint-passes
    severity: blocking
    description: 'golangci-lint passes via the Makefile target'
    command: 'make -O test_go_lint'

  - id: unit-tests-pass
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Unit tests pass (excludes test/cli)'
    command: 'make test_unit'

  - id: go-mod-in-sync
    severity: blocking
    description: 'All three go.mod files are tidy and on the same dependency versions'
    command: "make mod_tidy && git diff --exit-code -- go.mod go.sum docs/examples/kubo-as-a-library/go.mod docs/examples/kubo-as-a-library/go.sum test/dependencies/go.mod test/dependencies/go.sum"

  - id: no-external-replace-directive
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No committed replace directive pointing at boxo or any external module. In-repo replaces of github.com/ipfs/kubo or its sub-modules (github.com/ipfs/kubo/...) to a relative path are allowed'
    check: "grep -nE '^replace|=>' go.mod docs/examples/kubo-as-a-library/go.mod test/dependencies/go.mod mcp/*/go.mod 2>/dev/null | grep -vE 'github\\.com/ipfs/kubo(/[^ ]*)? => \\.'"

  - id: rpc-api-compatible
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No /api/v0 endpoint removed or renamed, no field renamed, no default changed, no response shape altered; same for core/coreiface interfaces'
    note: 'Manual review of core/commands, core/coreiface, client/rpc diffs; additive endpoints and optional arguments only'

  - id: gateway-conformance
    severity: blocking
    description: 'HTTP Gateway behavior stays spec-conformant'
    command: 'make build && PATH="$PWD/cmd/ipfs:$PATH" IPFS_PATH="$(mktemp -d)" go test ./test/cli/... -run "TestGateway" -v'
    note: 'CI also runs ipfs/gateway-conformance; never weaken its assertions'

  - id: default-cid-recipe-unchanged
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Default ipfs add recipe still matches unixfs-v0-2015'
    command: 'make build && PATH="$PWD/cmd/ipfs:$PATH" IPFS_PATH="$(mktemp -d)" go test ./test/cli/... -run "TestDefaultMatchesExpectedProfile" -v'

  - id: telemetry-opt-outs
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Telemetry honors IPFS_TELEMETRY=off, DO_NOT_TRACK and config opt-out; no new reporting path'
    command: 'make build && PATH="$PWD/cmd/ipfs:$PATH" IPFS_PATH="$(mktemp -d)" go test ./test/cli/... -run "TestTelemetry" -v'

  - id: no-silent-cid-injection
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Announcements follow local actions and Provide.Strategy; Provide.Enabled=false silences them. No feature (including MCP tools) adds, pins or provides CIDs without an operator-initiated local cause'
    command: 'make build && PATH="$PWD/cmd/ipfs:$PATH" IPFS_PATH="$(mktemp -d)" go test ./test/cli/... -run "TestProvider" -v'

  - id: no-tracking
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No code collects, logs or reports who runs a node, what it stores or requests, or whom it connects to; no deanonymization helpers'
    note: 'Manual review; applies to mcp/ server logging and MCP App views'

  - id: configurable-endpoints
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Every hardcoded URL, bootstrap peer, router, CA or shared service is configurable and can be turned off'
    check: "grep -rnE 'https?://' mcp/server mcp/app/src mcp/ui/src --include='*.go' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '_test\\.go|\\.test\\.tsx?|localhost|127\\.0\\.0\\.1|//\\s'"
    note: 'Each hit needs a config override and an off switch documented in docs'

  - id: feature-off-switch
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Every new feature or flipped default has an off switch, a docs/config.md (or mcp docs) entry, a changelog example, and tests with it disabled'
    note: 'Manual review at phase boundary'

  - id: no-resource-appropriation
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No default spending of operator CPU, bandwidth or storage for third parties; no monetization, crypto integration or decentralized-compute features without a prior AGENTS.md policy PR'
    note: 'Manual review'

  - id: protocol-change-needs-ipip
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Any wire/protocol change links an IPIP in ipfs/specs first'
    note: 'Manual review of bitswap, DHT, identify and other wire behavior'

  - id: protected-paths
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Do not modify test/sharness/lib/, .github/ (unless asked), auto-generated Changelog/Contributors sections in docs/changelogs/, version.go or release tooling'
    check: "git diff --name-only HEAD -- test/sharness/lib .github version.go bin/mkreleaselog"

  - id: no-new-sharness-tests
    severity: blocking
    description: 'New integration tests go in test/cli/, not test/sharness/'
    check: "git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A HEAD -- test/sharness"

  - id: no-hardcoded-secrets
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No hardcoded API keys, tokens or passwords; RPC credentials come from env or config'
    check: "grep -rnE '(api[_-]?key|secret|token|password)\\s*[:=]\\s*[\"\\x27][A-Za-z0-9_\\-]{12,}' mcp core cmd client config --include='*.go' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' 2>/dev/null | grep -v _test"

  - id: mcp-tool-annotations
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Every MCP tool declares readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/idempotentHint/openWorldHint matching mcp/contract; destructive tools follow the opt-in ADR'
    note: 'Verified by mcp/server contract tests once they exist'
```

---

## Warning Constraints (acknowledge before archiving)

```yaml
  - id: tests-for-new-features
    severity: warning
    description: 'New functionality and bug fixes carry tests; integration tests in test/cli use the harness and t.Context()'

  - id: cli-help-width
    severity: warning
    description: 'After editing help text in core/commands, help width stays within limits'
    command: 'make build && PATH="$PWD/cmd/ipfs:$PATH" IPFS_PATH="$(mktemp -d)" go test ./test/cli/... -run "TestCommandDocsWidth" -v'

  - id: config-docs
    severity: warning
    description: 'New or changed config options are documented in docs/config.md'

  - id: no-emojis
    severity: warning
    description: 'No emojis in code, comments, test names or log output'

  - id: agents-md-separate-pr
    severity: warning
    description: 'AGENTS.md changes ship in their own PR, never alongside code (upstream rule; relevant if anything is proposed upstream)'
    check: "git diff --name-only HEAD -- AGENTS.md"
    waiver: 'Waived by the operator on 2026-10-09 for the fork-only GQAdonis/kubo (operator-answers.md, answer 8): AGENTS.md is committed together with the ipfs-mcp-server changes. Reinstate before anything is proposed upstream.'

  - id: skills-spec-compliant
    severity: warning
    description: 'Skills under mcp/skills validate against agentskills.io (skills-ref validate)'

  - id: ui-accessibility
    severity: warning
    description: 'mcp/ui and mcp/app components meet WCAG 2.2 AA in light and dark themes'
    note: 'Reviewed by reviewer via prometheus-ui-review after the UI implementation phase'
```

---

## Workflow Triggers

```yaml
workflow_triggers:
  - event: on_iteration_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: 'make build'

  - event: on_change_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: 'make test_unit && make -O test_go_lint'
```

Commits are not automated; the operator commits, and `AGENTS.md` changes stay in their own commit.

``` ADDENDUM: ipfs-mcp-server (G9-G12) Project: Kubo (fork GQAdonis/kubo, 0.44.0-dev, HEAD 833e04a24) Date: 2026-10-09 Base: assessment.md revision 2 (decision of record F4, W1+W4), plan.md revision 2 (22 changes) Scope of this addendum: G9 AG-UI/A2A, G10 LLM backend, G11 chat UI, G12 embeddings/SurrealDB Revision: 3 (consolidation, 2026-10-09): the decision of record follows the round-2 adjudication and the operator answers of 2026-10-09; revision 2 followed review round 1 (BLOCK) ``` Assessor: `ipfs-agent-architect` (KBD Assess stage, addendum). The only file written is this one. No code, no OpenSpec change, and no file in another repository was touched. ### Revision 2 changes (review round 1) | Finding | How revision 2 addresses it | |---|---| | CRITICAL A: no falsifier; non-delivery defaulted to "ship non-conformant" | New section ASSUMPTIONS AND FALSIFIERS, per goal. The safe default on non-delivery is **defer**, never "ship non-conformant", with a dated delivery gate (end of Round 4). The N2 spike now tests the addendum's own top risks: an A2A-delegated write, setup cost against a threshold, and UAR behavior with and without the shipped profile. | | CRITICAL B: G10/G12 guarantees delegated to a runtime that breaks them by default | New section KUBO-SIDE ENFORCEMENT. Four things Kubo ships in `ipfs mcp`: a principal policy, an egress acknowledgement, an out-of-band confirmation channel, and a `check-uar` preflight. Kubo also ships a tested UAR profile under `mcp/uar/**`. Acceptance criteria are tied to these. Guarantees Kubo cannot enforce are named and the goal is marked **partially unmet** for them. "Nothing leaves the machine by default" is removed from ADR-0006. | | WARNING B: "the human gate holds today" over A2A | Claim removed. New evidence: UAR bypasses tool approval entirely when its governance gate is disabled. That is possible in loopback mode without JWT (`uar:src/uar/runtime/manager.rs:5469-5480`, `uar:src/uar/governance/runtime_control.rs:455-478, 662-663`). The A2A human gate is **unknown** until N2 proves it, and the Kubo-side out-of-band confirmation becomes the enforceable gate. | | WARNING C: G10 reinterpreted | The G10 decision is **PENDING operator question 2**. L3 (thin proxy) is re-presented with its real gain (a Kubo-controlled origin/auth boundary) and its real cost. | | WARNING D: scores without weights; (d) Security and Rules fit inflated | Weights and the aggregation rule are stated. Options with goal fit at or below 2 are excluded before aggregation. Every table is re-scored, (d) and E1 are scored "as shipped" and "with Kubo enforcement", and the margins and sensitivities are stated. | | WARNING E: G12 silently narrowed to UAR-routed content | Listed as an explicit limitation, with an opt-in `ipfs mcp` embedding hook as the option that closes it (N9, conditional). | | SUGGESTION: deletion checks remaining pins | Adopted. Vectors are deleted only when `pin ls --type=all ` shows no direct, recursive or indirect pin. On `repo_gc`, deletion is limited to CIDs that GC reports as removed. | | Consolidation (2026-10-09, after round 2 and the full cross-model review `findings.full.json`) | The DECISION and the ADR-0004 to ADR-0006 drafts are rewritten as the self-contained decision of record:
  • G9: topology A, AG-UI and A2A in `ipfs mcp` at default `127.0.0.1:5050`, with topology B (UAR-hosted) gated on a published UAR release by the end of Round 4
  • G10: L3, `ipfs mcp` proxies to an operator-configured UAR or OpenAI-compatible server
  • Human gate: native OS prompt with a presence factor
  • G11: Web UI island, Promethity, talking only to `ipfs mcp`; Desktop fork in scope
  • G12: requirements, concrete per-mode mechanisms and acceptance tests, with the component choice left to plan revision 2
Load-bearing assumptions and falsifiers now sit inside DECISION per goal. Stdio-spawned UAR is forbidden wherever node content reaches a model, and the general "nothing leaves the machine" claim is withdrawn and replaced by a stated partial guarantee. Plan impact is rewritten: 34 changes. The revision-2 DECISION, ADRs and plan impact are kept under "SUPERSEDED (2026-10-09)". The review sections at the end are unchanged. | Evidence conventions (same as `assessment.md`, plus two prefixes): - `path:line` is a Kubo working-tree fact read this session. - `uar:path:line` is from `/Users/gqadonis/Projects/prometheus/universal-agent-runtime` (HEAD `a7cb9729`, 2026-10-01), read-only. - `webui:path:line` is from `/Users/gqadonis/Projects/references/ipfs-webui` (HEAD `24ddaa89`), and `desktop:path:line` is from `/Users/gqadonis/Projects/references/ipfs-desktop` (HEAD `9bd9904`, origin `tribe-health/ipfs-desktop`). Both are read-only. - **[sub]** marks facts from read-only Explore sub-investigations run this session. The lead re-read these key ones and they hold: - `uar:src/uar/api/a2a/types.rs:116-132`, `uar:src/uar/api/a2a/mod.rs:75`, `uar:src/uar/api/a2a/agent_card.rs:26-30` - `uar:src/server.rs:2040-2051, 2528-2533` - `uar:src/config.rs:1409-1414, 1476` (no `cors` key in `uar:src/config.rs`: `grep -n cors` returns nothing) - `uar:src/uar/api/adapters.rs:361-381`, `uar:src/mcp/registry.rs:140-173` - `uar:src/uar/runtime/manager.rs:647-652, 5450-5510`, `uar:src/uar/governance/runtime_control.rs:455-478, 533, 662-663` - `uar:src/uar/api/a2a/task_execution.rs:568` - `webui:package.json:83, 91, 100, 104, 313-314`, `desktop:src/webui/index.js:41-47` - the greps for `elicit`, `ui://` and `RunAgentInput` in UAR `src` (no relevant hits; the only `elicit` match is the token "felicity" in a tokenizer JSON file) - **[external]** marks facts from outside the repositories, with the URL and the date fetched (2026-10-09). **[unverified]** marks claims that were not checked. --- > Review excerpt: lines 506-951 (DECISION, ADR DRAFTS, IMPACT, RISKS AND OPEN QUESTIONS) of assessment-addendum.md revision 3. Option analysis (107-382), enforcement (383-447) and falsifiers (448-505) are summarized inside DECISION; superseded revision-2 text (987+) is excluded. ## DECISION **Decision of record, revision 3 (consolidation, 2026-10-09).** This section is self-contained. It supersedes the revision-2 DECISION ("UAR-hosted primary"), which is kept unchanged under "SUPERSEDED (2026-10-09)" near the end of this file. Its basis: - the orchestrator adjudication of the round-2 CRITICAL, applied here: the addendum's own goal-fit gate excludes UAR-hosted (d) when undelivered UAR work is not credited, which leaves (a) at 51 against (c) at 49; - the operator's binding answers of 2026-10-09 (`operator-answers.md`, "Answers to the G9-G12 addendum"); - the orchestrator defaults for questions 3, 5 and 8-11 recorded there. **Shared principle (replaces the revision-2 principle).** `ipfs mcp` is the agentic surface of the node: - It serves MCP, AG-UI and A2A from one process. - It runs a minimal, bounded agent loop over contract tools only. - It proxies model calls to an operator-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint: UAR or any other server. - It reuses one `AuthVerifier`, one scope map and one confirmation gate in-process. The daemon, `/api/v0`, the gateway, `config/` and `docs/config.md` stay unchanged (F4). UAR is a supported LLM backend in topology A, and a second, gated topology (B) in which UAR hosts the agent endpoints. **This reverses one revision-2 claim, and the consequence is stated, not hidden:** Kubo's fork now contains an LLM HTTP client and a minimal agent loop. Both live inside `ipfs mcp`, behind the build tag `noagent` (and `nomcp`). There is no default endpoint, and nothing is mounted unless configured. ### G9: topology A, AG-UI and A2A served by `ipfs mcp`; topology B (UAR-hosted) is gated **Topology A (primary, delivered this phase).** - **Listener.** - `ipfs mcp --http` gains AG-UI and A2A on the same listener as MCP Streamable HTTP, on distinct paths: `/mcp`, `/agui`, `/a2a`, and `/.well-known/agent-card.json`. - The listener's default address is **`127.0.0.1:5050`**, overridable with `--http=`. - Port 4000 is never used as a default; it is the local liter-llm gateway port in this environment and would collide. - Kubo's defaults 4001, 5001 and 8080 are not used either. - The F4 bind rules carry over: a non-loopback bind is refused without a configured verifier. - **AG-UI.** - `POST /agui` accepts `RunAgentInput` and streams spec events over SSE. - A pending confirmation ends the run with `RUN_FINISHED` `outcome: {type: "interrupt", interrupts: [...]}` (https://docs.ag-ui.com/concepts/interrupts, fetched 2026-10-09). - The resume input carries `resume: [{interruptId, status, payload}]`. - **A2A 1.0.** - The agent card lives at `/.well-known/agent-card.json`, with the JSON-RPC binding at `/a2a`: `message/send`, `message/stream`, `tasks/get`, `tasks/cancel`. - A pending confirmation is `TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED`, and a missing or insufficient credential is `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED`. - The skills are generated from the contract's A2A skill metadata. - **In-process reuse.** - All three protocols authenticate through the same `AuthVerifier` and authorize through the same scope map. - A tool call from AG-UI or A2A goes through the same confirmation gate as an MCP call. - **Off switches.** - `--agui` and `--a2a` are off by default. - They are mounted only when an LLM backend is configured (G10). - `noagent` compiles them out. - **Protocol implementation.** The plan prefers hand-written types generated from the spec schemas over `net/http`, with no new SDK. An SDK (a2a-go v2, a community AG-UI Go SDK) is taken only if plan revision 2 measures its dependency weight and the operator accepts it; operator answer 2 covered go-sdk only. **Topology B (second supported topology, gated).** - **What it is.** UAR hosts AG-UI and A2A, and calls `ipfs mcp --http` as a configured principal (kind `uar`) with read-only default groups, `egress_ack`, the native confirmation prompt, and `check-uar`. - **Stdio is forbidden.** Stdio-spawned UAR is forbidden for topology B. Over stdio, `ipfs mcp` cannot identify the client or enforce egress. - The shipped profile never spawns `ipfs mcp`. - `ipfs mcp` refuses `contentEgress` tools to a stdio client whose MCP `clientInfo` identifies UAR. This is a misconfiguration guard, not a security boundary, because `clientInfo` is self-reported. - **Delivery gate.** B is supported only if UAR's conformance items are **contained in a published, installable UAR release (tag plus image digest or native package) by the end of Round 4**: agent card at `agent-card.json`, A2A 1.0 TaskState wire values, approval surfaced as input-required, `RunAgentInput` with spec interrupts, a configurable CORS allowlist, and safe defaults. - **Version pin.** The shipped `mcp/uar/profile/` pins that minimum UAR version, and `check-uar` refuses older versions via the agent card. - **If the gate fails:** topology B is deferred and reported unmet. There is no non-conformant B release. G9 is still delivered through topology A. **Assumptions and falsifiers (G9).** Each row's observable is measurable; the default on falsification is the safe one. | # | Assumption | Falsifier (observable) | Consequence | |---|---|---|---| | G9-1 | AG-UI and A2A can be served conformantly from `ipfs mcp` without an SDK | Plan revision 2's conformance tests (AG-UI event schema validation against the published `@ag-ui/core` schemas; A2A JSON-RPC schema validation against `a2aproject/A2A` 1.0 JSON schema) fail and cannot be fixed within the change | Take the SDK (operator approval of the root `go.mod` addition), or ship A2A only and defer AG-UI | | G9-2 | A2A-delegated writes cannot run without a human | A test peer agent's `message/send` asks for `pin_add`, and the pin exists before a human approves the native prompt | Block: write groups are refused to every A2A principal until fixed | | G9-3 | Topology B's UAR fixes ship in a published release by the end of Round 4 | No UAR tag or image digest containing all listed items exists at the end of Round 4 | Topology B deferred and reported unmet; A unaffected | | G9-4 | The single `--http` listener can carry MCP, AG-UI and A2A without cross-protocol auth confusion | A token scoped for one protocol's principal is accepted on another protocol's path for a tool outside its groups (`test/cli` matrix) | Block until fixed; separate listeners if needed | ### G10: L3, `ipfs mcp` proxies model calls to an operator-configured UAR instance or OpenAI-compatible server - **The loop.** - The agent loop for topology A runs in `ipfs mcp`. - It is minimal: a step limit, a token budget and a wall-clock limit, all configurable with conservative defaults. - Its tools are only the contract tools enabled for the calling principal. - It has no shell, no filesystem and no network tools. - **The model endpoint.** The model is reached over the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API (`POST /chat/completions` with `tools`). Both UAR (`/v1/chat/completions`, `uar:src/server.rs:1901`) [sub] and other OpenAI-compatible servers provide it. - **Configuration.** - `--llm-base-url`, `--llm-model` and `--llm-api-key-env=` (or `--llm-api-key-file`), or the same keys in the `ipfs mcp` config file. - **There is no default URL and no default model.** - The key is read from the named env var or file, never accepted as a literal. - Unset means G9/G10 surfaces are not mounted and no model call is ever made. - **Egress, enforced in-process.** - A tool result marked `contentEgress` (`ipfs_cat`, `ipfs_get`, `dag_get`, `ipfs_ls` and others) is included in a model request only if the backend's host is listed in `egress_ack`. - Otherwise the loop returns a structured refusal to the model and the user ("Content not sent: `` is not in egress_ack."). - With a UAR backend, `check-uar` also verifies UAR's effective upstream provider (re-checked per session and when UAR's settings report a change) where its settings API exposes it. - **Remaining partial guarantee (limitation).** Kubo cannot verify what an acknowledged endpoint does with data. The cases: - a loopback server that forwards upstream; - a UAR whose effective provider is not readable; - stdio MCP hosts (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) that send tool results to their own models; - WebMCP tools executing in the browser. The operator's `egress_ack` is the control, and docs state this. **This addendum does not claim "no content leaves the machine" in general.** **Assumptions and falsifiers (G10).** | # | Assumption | Falsifier (observable) | Consequence | |---|---|---|---| | G10-1 | UAR's `/v1/chat/completions` accepts client-supplied `tools` and returns `tool_calls` without executing its own tools | The integration test against a UAR built from the pinned published release shows UAR executing a tool itself, or dropping client tools | UAR as a G10 backend is unsupported until fixed. OpenAI-compatible servers remain. | | G10-2 | At least one local OpenAI-compatible server supports tool calling well enough for the contract tools | The real-service test with one named local server (chosen in plan revision 2) fails the tool-call round trip | G10 is local-unmet; a remote backend with `egress_ack` is still supported. Reported. | | G10-3 | No model call happens without configuration | `test/cli`: with no `--llm-*` set, `/agui` and `/a2a` return 404, and a network capture shows zero outbound connections from `ipfs mcp` | Block | | G10-4 | `egress_ack` is enforced for every `contentEgress` result | `test/cli` with a fake model server: content from `ipfs_cat` reaches the model request body without its host in `egress_ack` | Block | | G10-5 | The UAR backend setup is acceptable | Measured from published artifacts on clean macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64: more than 30 minutes or more than 15 steps (threshold per operator default for question 11) | The UAR backend is documented as "advanced". OpenAI-compatible local servers are the recommended path. | ### Human gate (applies to G9, G10, G11 and topology B) - **Priority order.** For clients that can elicit, MCP elicitation stays the primary gate. For every principal that cannot elicit, the gate is a **native OS prompt**: - an IPFS Desktop confirmation window, when Desktop is running and paired with `ipfs mcp` over a local authenticated channel; - otherwise a macOS or Linux system prompt raised by `ipfs mcp`. Both show the tool, the CID, path or name, and the effect. - **Human presence.** The prompt must require presence that a same-user background process cannot simulate. Candidate mechanisms, chosen in plan revision 2 and verified by the falsifier below: - macOS LocalAuthentication (Touch ID or password); - a Linux polkit authentication agent; - for Desktop, a window that requires a user gesture and is not reachable through the Web UI's renderer. - **Headless only.** `ipfs mcp confirm ` exists only for headless servers behind an explicit opt-in (`--confirm=cli`). It checks for a TTY and prints, at startup and per request, that same-user processes can reach it. - **Shell-capable tools.** They are refused for principals with write scope. - In topology A, the loop exposes no shell tools. - In topology B, `check-uar` refuses write groups when UAR reports `terminal_exec` enabled (`uar:src/uar/tools/terminal_exec.rs:22-27`, opt-in at `uar:src/config.rs:2523-2525`, per the round-2 finding) or any configured MCP server other than `ipfs mcp`. - The shipped profile pins `terminal_exec` off. - **AG-UI chat interrupts.** An interrupt answered in the chat island counts as the human gate for the chat principal (kind `ui`), the same way elicitation does. Destructive tools additionally raise the native prompt. This default is revisited if G11-3 is falsified. - **Expiry.** An expired or unanswered prompt is a denial ("Deny is final."). **Assumptions and falsifiers (human gate).** | # | Assumption | Falsifier (observable) | Consequence | |---|---|---|---| | HG-1 | A same-user process cannot approve a pending write | Test: an agent with shell access (topology B UAR with `terminal_exec` enabled in a test-only profile, and a plain same-user script) tries to approve via AppleScript/`System Events`, `xdotool`, the control socket or the Desktop channel, and succeeds | Block that mechanism. Fall back to the presence-factor mechanism or refuse writes for non-elicitation principals on that platform. | | HG-2 | `check-uar` sees UAR's tool inventory | The UAR settings or tools API does not expose `terminal_exec` or the MCP server list from the pinned release | Write groups are refused to topology-B principals (fail closed) | ### G11: React 19 island in the Web UI fork, Promethity, talking only to `ipfs mcp`; Desktop fork in scope - **The `mcp/chat` package.** - A shadow-root custom element (React 19, Tailwind 4, shadcn, the A2UI renderer from `mcp/ui`, an AG-UI client), with Promethity tokens and fonts bundled. - No remote assets, no `unsafe-eval`. - **Mount.** It is mounted in the GQAdonis/ipfs-webui fork behind an off-by-default Settings toggle and loaded by dynamic import. Desktop gets it through the bundled Web UI (D1). - **Backend.** - The island talks **only** to `ipfs mcp --http` `/agui`, **never** to UAR. - `ipfs mcp` enforces an origin allowlist: `webui://localhost`, `http://127.0.0.1:5001`, `http://localhost:5001`, plus configured subdomain-gateway origins. - The chat principal is kind `ui`, with its own bearer token. - **Desktop:** the token is held by the main process with `safeStorage` and attached via a preload bridge, so it is never in page storage. - **Browser `/webui`:** the user enters it once, and it is held per-origin. This is the stated admin-origin risk, accepted by the operator. - **Desktop fork (tribe-health/ipfs-desktop), in scope this phase.** - Owned by ui-ux-engineer, reviewed by security-reviewer. - It adds a CSP for `webui://localhost` whose `connect-src` lists the RPC and `ipfs mcp` origins. - It re-enables `webSecurity` (`desktop:src/webui/index.js:41-47`). - It adds the `safeStorage` key bridge. - It adds the Desktop confirmation window and its local channel to `ipfs mcp` (human gate). **Assumptions and falsifiers (G11).** | # | Assumption | Falsifier (observable) | Consequence | |---|---|---|---| | G11-1 | The shadow root isolates Tailwind 4 from Tachyons in browsers and Electron 44 | Visual regression: any Web UI page differs with the island loaded and closed, or the island renders unstyled in Electron 44 | Desktop-only side view (U3) for this phase | | G11-2 | Re-enabling `webSecurity` and adding the CSP does not break Desktop | Desktop smoke test (files, explore, peers, settings, add, pin) fails with the change | Fix allowlists. Never ship with `webSecurity: false` restored silently; report the regression. | | G11-3 | Chat interrupts can only be resolved by a user gesture | Security review or test shows script in the page resolves an interrupt without a user gesture | Require the native prompt for all chat writes | | G11-4 | The admin-origin exposure is bounded | Security review finds the island bundle loads any remote resource, or the `ipfs mcp` token is readable from Desktop page storage | Block | ### G12: requirements, mechanisms and falsifiers stated; the component choice is made by plan revision 2's re-score **G12 is not decided beyond this section.** The adjudication found that revision 2's E1 goal-fit score has the same defect as (d). Plan revision 2 re-scores G12 under the goal-fit gate and chooses which component performs embedding and storage: `ipfs mcp`, or UAR in topology B. **Requirements** (binding, from G12 and the operator defaults): - off by default; - operator-configured embedding provider, local or remote, never a hardcoded endpoint; - a remote embedder needs `egress_ack`; - both embedded and remote SurrealDB modes; - chunking, model, dimension, content types and trigger are configurable; - storage keyed by CID; - pin-aware deletion; - no daemon-wide hook (E5 refused). **Remote mode, concrete.** Either: - `ipfs mcp` connects with `github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb.go`; - v1.7.0, published 2026-09-07 per `proxy.golang.org/.../@latest`; - Apache-2.0 per its `LICENSE`; - its `go.mod` requires only pure-Go modules (`fxamacker/cbor/v2`, `gorilla/websocket`, `lxzan/gws`, `golang-jwt/jwt/v5`, `gofrs/uuid`) [external, fetched 2026-10-09; cgo-freeness of the full build is unverified until plan revision 2 builds it]; - the URL and namespace/database come from config, and credentials come from env or file; - or UAR's remote configuration (`config.remote.surreal.yaml`) in topology B. **Embedded mode, concrete.** Either: - **(i) a managed local `surreal` process.** - `ipfs mcp` starts `surreal start --bind 127.0.0.1: surrealkv://` with credentials generated per start, and stops it on exit. It connects with `surrealdb.go`. - It runs only when embedded mode is configured. - The `surreal` binary path is operator-configured. Kubo never downloads it or ships it (BSL 1.1 stays outside Kubo's artifacts). - **or (ii) UAR-embedded surrealkv** (`uar:src/config.rs:1439-1440`) in topology B. `surrealdb.c.go` (cgo plus a Rust native library) is excluded: Kubo has no cgo. **Embedding computation.** Either: - an operator-configured OpenAI-compatible `/embeddings` endpoint called by `ipfs mcp` (a local server, or UAR's endpoint if it exposes one [unverified]); - or UAR's FastEmbed in topology B. There is no default. **Trigger.** - On a successful `ipfs_add` from any `ipfs mcp` transport (stdio, HTTP, AG-UI chat, A2A), when indexing is configured. - Subject to the MIME allowlist and a size cap. - Plus an explicit "index this CID" tool. - **Limitation:** WebMCP tools in the browser call the RPC directly, not through `ipfs mcp`, so content they add is not indexed unless re-indexed explicitly. **Deletion.** - Delete a CID's vectors only when `pin ls --type=all ` reports no direct, recursive or indirect pin. - On `repo_gc`, only for CIDs that GC reports as removed. - Operator-triggered reconciliation for content unpinned outside `ipfs mcp`. **Acceptance tests per mode** (plan revision 2 turns them into tasks): | Mode | Test | |---|---| | Disabled (default) | No `surreal` process spawned. No connection to any store or embedder (network capture). Index tools absent. | | Embedded (i) | Start and stop lifecycle, including crash cleanup. Loopback-only bind. Data under the configured directory. Ingest, then search, then pin-aware delete against a harness daemon. Zero outbound connections with a local embedder. | | Embedded (ii) / remote via UAR (topology B only) | The same flow through the pinned UAR release, gated like topology B. | | Remote (surrealdb.go) | ws/wss URL from config, credentials from env, the same flow against a real `surreal` server started by the test. Refusal when the embedder host is not in `egress_ack`. | **Assumptions and falsifiers (G12).** | # | Assumption | Falsifier (observable) | Consequence | |---|---|---|---| | G12-1 | `surrealdb.go` builds into `ipfs` without cgo and at an acceptable size | `CGO_ENABLED=0 make build` fails with it, or the measured binary delta exceeds the limit plan revision 2 sets | Remote and embedded (i) via `ipfs mcp` are unsupported; topology B only, or G12 deferred | | G12-2 | SurrealDB vector search (HNSW) works for the configured dimension via `surrealdb.go` | A real-service test cannot define or query an HNSW index from Go | In-memory fallback is not accepted; G12 deferred | | G12-3 | The managed process can be supervised safely | The test leaves an orphaned `surreal` process after `ipfs mcp` is killed, or it binds non-loopback | Embedded (i) unsupported until fixed | | G12-4 | Deletion stays consistent with the pin state | A CID pinned twice (recursive root and direct) loses its vectors when one pin is removed | Block | --- ## ADR DRAFTS The plan stage materializes these in `docs/mcp/`, after ADR-0001 to ADR-0003. The revision-2 drafts are kept under "SUPERSEDED (2026-10-09)". ### ADR-0004 draft: AG-UI and A2A are served by `ipfs mcp`, and model calls are proxied to an operator-configured endpoint - **Status:** Proposed, decision of record per operator answers (2026-10-09). Accepted once plan revision 2 is approved. - **Context.** - G9 and G10. - F4 keeps Kubo's agent surface in `ipfs mcp` (RPC-only, no daemon change). - AGENTS.md: no default endpoints, an off switch for every feature, no tracking. - UAR (MIT) is non-conformant to A2A 1.0/AG-UI today, and its approval can be bypassed when governance is disabled (Summary 2, 4). - The goal-fit gate excludes UAR-hosted endpoints while UAR's fixes are undelivered (adjudication). - The operator chose "Both". - **Decision.** - **Topology A.** `ipfs mcp --http` (default `127.0.0.1:5050`) serves AG-UI (`/agui`, spec interrupts) and A2A 1.0 (`/.well-known/agent-card.json`, `/a2a`, input-required and auth-required). Both reuse the `AuthVerifier`, the scope map and the confirmation gate in-process. - **The loop and the model.** A bounded loop over contract tools calls an operator-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint (UAR or another server). There is no default URL or model, and the key comes from env or file. - **Egress.** `contentEgress` results reach a model only for hosts in `egress_ack`. - **Human gate.** For non-eliciting clients, a native OS prompt with a presence factor. CLI confirm is headless opt-in only. Shell-capable tools are refused for write principals. - **Topology B.** UAR-hosted, over `--http` only, with stdio forbidden. Supported once UAR's fixes ship in a published release by the end of Round 4; otherwise deferred and reported unmet. - **Off switches.** `--agui`/`--a2a` are off by default and mounted only with a configured backend; `noagent` compiles them out. - **Consequences.** - **Positive:** conformance is under this team's control; one gate and one auth path; works with any OpenAI-compatible server, local or remote; UAR is optional. - **Negative:** - The fork now carries an LLM client and a minimal agent loop (maintenance in this repo). - Possible new root `go.mod` modules if an SDK is taken (G9-1). - The egress guarantee is limited to what `egress_ack` and `check-uar` can see. - Native prompts need per-OS implementations. - **Rejected or deferred alternatives:** | Alternative | Rejected or deferred because | |---|---| | (d) UAR-hosted as primary | Excluded by the goal-fit gate while UAR's fixes are undelivered. Kept as topology B. | | (b) daemon listener | C1 plus an LLM client in the daemon | | (c) separate binary | A second product in the repo | | L1 UAR-only backend | Fails G10's "or an OpenAI-compatible server" | | Token fallback or a 0600 socket as the human gate | Reachable by same-user processes (round-2 finding) | | Stdio-spawned UAR | Egress unenforceable | ### ADR-0005 draft: chat UI as a React 19 island in the Web UI fork, talking only to `ipfs mcp`; Desktop hardened - **Status:** Proposed, decision of record per operator answers (2026-10-09). - **Context.** - G11. - The Web UI is React 16 / CRA 5 / Tachyons with React-capped dependencies (Summary 6). - The Web UI origin holds admin RPC. - Desktop has no CSP and runs `webSecurity: false`. - The operator chose the Web UI island, Promethity, and the Desktop fork in scope. - **Decision.** - `mcp/chat` is a shadow-root React 19 element (Tailwind 4, shadcn, A2UI, an AG-UI client, Promethity), mounted off by default in the Web UI fork and reaching Desktop through D1. - It talks only to `ipfs mcp` `/agui`, behind an origin allowlist and a `ui` principal token. - In the Desktop fork: CSP, `webSecurity` re-enabled, a `safeStorage` token bridge, and the native confirmation window. - Owner: ui-ux-engineer. Reviewer: security-reviewer. - **Consequences.** - **Positive:** the fork stays near upstream; one component set; brand control; no browser credential to UAR. - **Negative:** - The chat runs in the admin origin (operator-accepted risk, bounded by G11-3/G11-4). - Two React copies when enabled. - Desktop fork divergence (CSP, `webSecurity`). - **Rejected alternatives:** | Alternative | Rejected because | |---|---| | U1 upgrade the fork | Rewrite-sized | | U3 Desktop-only | Leaves browser users out. It is the flip if G11-1 fails. | | U4 iframe UAR | Not IPFS-specific | | Direct-to-UAR from the browser | UAR CORS is not configurable; the operator chose "never directly to UAR" | ### ADR-0006 draft: G12 requirements and mechanisms; component choice deferred to plan revision 2 - **Status:** Proposed, requirements only. The component choice (`ipfs mcp` or UAR topology B) is recorded by plan revision 2's re-score under the goal-fit gate. This ADR does not claim G12 decided. - **Context.** - G12 requires both embedded and remote SurrealDB, an operator-configured embedder, off by default. - Embedded SurrealDB from Go via `surrealdb.c.go` needs cgo; Kubo has none. - `surrealdb.go` v1.7.0 is an Apache-2.0 network client. - The SurrealDB engine is BSL 1.1. - Kubo has no pin-removal event stream. - **Decision.** - **Remote mode:** `surrealdb.go` from `ipfs mcp`, or UAR remote config (topology B). - **Embedded mode:** a managed local `surreal` process (surrealkv, loopback, operator-provided binary, started and stopped by `ipfs mcp` only when configured), or UAR-embedded surrealkv (topology B). - **Embedding:** an operator-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint or UAR FastEmbed. There is no default, and a remote embedder needs `egress_ack`. - **Trigger:** `ipfs_add` through `ipfs mcp` or an explicit index tool. - **Deletion:** pin-aware. - **Refused:** a daemon-wide hook. Excluded: cgo. - **Consequences.** - **Positive:** no cgo and no BSL code in Kubo artifacts; both modes have a concrete mechanism and per-mode acceptance tests. - **Negative:** - Kubo (`ipfs mcp`) may supervise a third-party process (embedded (i)). - WebMCP-added content is not indexed automatically. - Content unpinned outside `ipfs mcp` stays indexed until reconciliation. - Egress for a remote embedder is limited to the `egress_ack` control. --- ## IMPACT ON F4 AND THE CURRENT PLAN This section replaces the revision-2 plan impact (kept under "SUPERSEDED (2026-10-09)"). ### F4 itself - **Placement unchanged.** `ipfs mcp` stays a local, RPC-only command. - **Additions inside `ipfs mcp`:** - the `--http` default address `127.0.0.1:5050`; - AG-UI and A2A routes; - a bounded agent loop and an OpenAI-compatible client; - principal policy, `egress_ack`, the native confirmation prompt and `check-uar`; - optional G12 indexing with a managed `surreal` process or a remote client. - **Build tag.** `noagent` removes everything except MCP. - **Still unchanged:** the daemon, `config/`, `docs/config.md`, `/api/v0` and the gateway. - **Possible new root `go.mod` modules:** `surrealdb.go` (G12) and a protocol SDK only if G9-1 requires one. Operator answer 2 covered go-sdk only, so plan revision 2 must get explicit approval for each. ### Changes to existing plan items (22) | # | Change | Impact | |---|---|---| | 0 | team-ownership-grant | Add grants:

The default on non-delivery is now deferral, which means **G9-G12 may deliver nothing in this phase**. That is the honest cost of the safe default. 2. **Setup cost.** It is measured in N2 against an explicit threshold (A10.2). If it fails, the principle itself is in question, and L2 becomes the likely answer. 3. **UAR's unsafe and non-configurable defaults.** - `0.0.0.0`, the remote model, the remote memory embedder, CORS `Any` (not configurable) and the governance bypass in local mode. - N8 enforces the node-data boundary only. This is documented as outside the guarantee, which is the same position as every other stdio MCP host today. 6. **`check-uar` couples Kubo to UAR's settings API shape.** A UAR release that changes it makes the principal fail closed, which is safe but disruptive. A10.3 records whether verification is possible at all. 7. **Chat in the admin origin.** Through the L3 proxy, the key is no longer in the browser, but an XSS in the island is still admin RPC. 8. **Embeddings drift and coverage.** Index drift from out-of-agent unpins, and non-UAR surfaces are not indexed without N9. 9. **SurrealDB BSL 1.1** is inherited by UAR deployers. 10. **The weighted margins for G9 and G11 are not decisive.** The decisions rest on qualitative arguments (maintenance location, reach) that a reasonable operator could weigh differently. ### Questions only the operator can answer > **Answered 2026-10-09.** > > - Q1, Q2, Q4, Q6 and Q7 by the operator (binding). > - Q3, Q5 and Q8-Q11 by orchestrator defaults the operator may overrule. > > See `operator-answers.md` and the appended "Answers to the G9-G12 addendum". The questions are kept as asked. New open items for plan revision 2: > > - approval of any new root `go.mod` modules (`surrealdb.go`, any protocol SDK); > - the G12 component choice from the re-score; > - the local OpenAI-compatible server used for G10-2. 1. **UAR as a required component.** Do you accept UAR as the runtime for G9-G12, with Kubo adding the N8 enforcement but no LLM client, vector store or chat backend? A "no" moves to (a)+L2 for G9/G10 and to E3 or deferral for G12. 2. **G10 narrowing.** Should "OpenAI-compatible server plus key" run through UAR (L1, narrows G10), through a Go loop in `ipfs mcp` (L2, about +2 changes), or behind an `ipfs mcp` proxy (L3, +1 change, also the G11 browser boundary)? 3. **Delivery gate.** The default at the end of Round 4, if UAR has not delivered the conformance items, is to defer G9 conformance and report it unmet. Do you instead want, in advance, the Kubo fallback (a) or an explicitly non-conformant release? 4. **Out-of-band confirmation.** Is a local CLI (`ipfs mcp confirm`) plus a loopback confirmation page acceptable as the human gate for agents without elicitation, including UAR? That reverses the plan's cut of this channel for these principals. 5. **Egress.** Is per-principal `egress_ack` (naming the model and embedder hosts) the right control, and should content tools stay refused for every non-elicitation principal without it? 6. **Chat placement and brand.** Web UI island (reaching Desktop) or Desktop-only (U3)? Promethity or IPFS-family branding inside the Web UI? 7. **Desktop fork.** Is `tribe-health/ipfs-desktop` in scope for this phase (CSP, key bridge)? Which role owns it? 8. **Embedding scope.** Embed only UAR-routed agent actions, or also enable the opt-in N9 hook so content added from stdio hosts, the MCP App and WebMCP is indexed? And is the pin-aware deletion plus operator-triggered reconciliation acceptable? 9. **SurrealDB license.** Is SurrealDB's BSL 1.1 acceptable for your deployments, through UAR? 10. **Remote modes.** Are a remote SurrealDB or a remote embedder needed this phase, or is local-only enough? 11. **Setup threshold.** Is the setup-cost threshold in A10.2 (30 minutes or 15 steps from published artifacts) the right falsifier, or do you want a different number? ---

**Decision of record, revision 3 (consolidation, 2026-10-09).** This section is self-contained. It supersedes the revision-2 DECISION ("UAR-hosted primary"), which is kept unchanged under "SUPERSEDED (2026-10-09)" near the end of this file. Its basis:

- the orchestrator adjudication of the round-2 CRITICAL, applied here: the addendum's own goal-fit gate excludes UAR-hosted (d) when undelivered UAR work is not credited, which leaves (a) at 51 against (c) at 49;
- the operator's binding answers of 2026-10-09 (`operator-answers.md`, "Answers to the G9-G12 addendum");
- the orchestrator defaults for questions 3, 5 and 8-11 recorded there.

**Shared principle (replaces the revision-2 principle).** `ipfs mcp` is the agentic surface of the node:

- It serves MCP, AG-UI and A2A from one process.
- It runs a minimal, bounded agent loop over contract tools only.
- It proxies model calls to an operator-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint: UAR or any other server.
- It reuses one `AuthVerifier`, one scope map and one confirmation gate in-process.

The daemon, `/api/v0`, the gateway, `config/` and `docs/config.md` stay unchanged (F4). UAR is a supported LLM backend in topology A, and a second, gated topology (B) in which UAR hosts the agent endpoints.

**This reverses one revision-2 claim, and the consequence is stated, not hidden:** Kubo's fork now contains an LLM HTTP client and a minimal agent loop. Both live inside `ipfs mcp`, behind the build tag `noagent` (and `nomcp`). There is no default endpoint, and nothing is mounted unless configured.

# Goals

- G1 Architecture decision by assessment with adversarial review: evaluate every placement for MCP support (ipfs CLI subcommand, separate binary/module over the RPC API, daemon-hosted endpoint alongside RPC/gateway, plugin, out-of-tree package, other) against Kubo stability and user-agency rules, security, distribution and maintenance cost; record the chosen option and rejected alternatives as an ADR
- G2 MCP server exposing IPFS operations to agents (add/get/cat, pinning, IPNS publish/resolve and keys, MFS, DAG, CAR import/export, routing/provide, node status) with accurate tool annotations and structured output, driven by one shared tool contract in mcp/contract
- G3 Transports: stdio for local agents and Streamable HTTP for remote use, with authentication, loopback-by-default binding, Origin/DNS-rebinding protection, and an off switch for every capability
- G4 MCP App with UI/UX: React 19 component library that is also an A2UI v0.9 catalog, served as ui:// resources, WCAG 2.2 AA, light and dark
- G5 agentskills.io-compliant skills for push/pull, pinning, IPNS, MFS, DAG/CAR and troubleshooting, packaged as plugins and marketplaces for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Kimi Code
- G6 No break to /api/v0, the HTTP gateway, the default CID recipe or wire compatibility; no tracking; no silent CID injection; destructive operations gated; docs and tests for every feature and its disabled state
- G7 Work is executed by the kubo-ipfs-agentic agent team with independent security and quality review at the phase boundary
- G8 WebMCP support in the IPFS Web UI (ipfs-webui): register IPFS tools via WebMCP (`document.modelContext`, with `navigator.modelContext` fallback) so agents in any WebMCP-capable host (Kimi desktop, Codex desktop, Chrome origin trial, other containers/browsers) can use the node through the Web UI; assess placement (ipfs-webui fork vs injected script vs Desktop wrapper), how Kubo/Desktop pin and serve the resulting Web UI CID, reuse of the shared tool contract, feature detection and an off switch, and host support evidence

- G9 AG-UI and A2A endpoints for the IPFS services, so agents and agent UIs can drive IPFS agentically (streamed AG-UI events for interactive UIs; A2A for agent-to-agent delegation); assess placement (daemon, `ipfs mcp` process, separate service, UAR-hosted), auth, and how they reuse the shared tool contract and confirmation gate
- G10 LLM backend for agentic behavior behind the AG-UI/A2A endpoints: proxy to an operator-configured Universal Agent Runtime instance (`/Users/gqadonis/Projects/prometheus/universal-agent-runtime`) or an operator-configured OpenAI-compatible server with API key; no default endpoint, off unless configured, credentials never hardcoded
- G11 Chat interface in IPFS Desktop and the IPFS Web UI: a right-side sliding shadcn/ui sidebar for AI chat about and with the user's node, rendering A2UI components wherever appropriate (shared A2UI catalog from mcp/ui), with tool calls subject to the same confirmation gate

- G12 Embeddings for uploaded documents: optional, configuration-driven automatic embedding of content added through the agent surfaces (chunking, model and dimension choice, which content types, when to embed), stored in SurrealDB with vector search, supporting both embedded and remote SurrealDB modes; off unless configured, embedding providers operator-configured (local or remote, never a hardcoded endpoint), and no content leaves the machine without explicit operator configuration
